gre-readiness-check-verbal-001.prompt: The conservator's field notes on the altarpiece were so _______ that later restorers could not _______ which varnish layers she had already lifted.

options.a: elliptical ... ascertain
options.b: exhaustive ... dispute
options.c: celebratory ... overlook
options.d: pedestrian ... applaud

gre-readiness-check-verbal-001.explanation: Sparse, sketchy notes would leave later restorers unable to determine what had already been removed. Elliptical (leaving out essential detail) plus ascertain (establish with certainty) matches that causal link.

distractorExplanations.b: Exhaustive notes would supply more, not less, information; dispute also fails the 'could not determine' logic.
distractorExplanations.c: Celebratory tone is irrelevant to missing technical detail; overlook does not mean 'fail to determine.'
distractorExplanations.d: Pedestrian means commonplace, not incomplete; applaud inverts the restorers' practical problem.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-002.prompt: Despite a public pose of _______, the mayor's private memos were crowded with grudges and planned score-settling.

options.a: rancor
options.b: magnanimity
options.c: petulance
options.d: irascibility

gre-readiness-check-verbal-002.explanation: Despite signals a contrast with the grudging memos. Magnanimity (generosity of spirit, refusal to nurse resentment) is the public mask that those memos contradict.

distractorExplanations.a: Rancor is bitter ill will; that would match the memos, not contrast with them.
distractorExplanations.c: Petulance is peevish irritability; it aligns with grudges rather than opposing them.
distractorExplanations.d: Irascibility is a hot temper; it names the memos' mood, not the generous public pose.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-003.prompt: A textile historian notes that a highland workshop kept indigo vats for decades yet bought no imported cakes of dye. Local plants yield a weaker blue, but surviving account books show only wages, firewood, and vat lime—no dye purchases. The passage most strongly supports which inference?

options.a: The workshop never produced commercially salable cloth.
options.b: Imported indigo cakes were chemically identical to local plants.
options.c: The workshop likely extracted dye from plants grown nearby.
options.d: Firewood costs prove the vats were used only for display.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-003.explanation: Long-running vats plus no dye purchases, while local plants can yield blue, point to on-site extraction rather than imported cakes. The books list operating costs, not a reason the vats were unused.

distractorExplanations.a: Overreaches: missing dye purchases do not show the cloth failed to sell.
distractorExplanations.b: The passage never compares chemical identity of imported cakes and local plants.
distractorExplanations.d: Firewood is an operating cost of heating vats, not evidence they were theatrical props.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-004.prompt: In a review of a climate bill, a columnist writes that the senator 'hedged every pledge until the floor vote.' In this context, hedged most nearly means

options.a: planted a physical barrier around the chamber
options.b: increased the numerical size of each pledge
options.c: shifted the debate onto agricultural subsidies
options.d: qualified each promise so it could later be walked back

gre-readiness-check-verbal-004.explanation: In political prose, to hedge a pledge is to surround it with caveats that preserve an exit. That figurative sense, not gardening or farm policy, fits 'until the floor vote.'

distractorExplanations.a: Takes the garden sense of hedge; the column is about legislative language, not landscaping.
distractorExplanations.b: Hedging does not mean enlarging a promise; it means narrowing or protecting it.
distractorExplanations.c: Confuses hedge with a pivot to farm subsidies; the stem is about how pledges were worded.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-005.prompt: The patent examiner's rejection is weakest where she fails to _______ that prior art, not the applicant's drawings, may be the _______ reason the claim lacks novelty.

options.a: consider ... principal
options.b: dismiss ... trivial
options.c: celebrate ... cosmetic
options.d: invent ... imaginary

gre-readiness-check-verbal-005.explanation: An argument is weak if it never takes seriously the leading alternative explanation. Consider plus principal names that omitted, central possibility.

distractorExplanations.b: Dismissing prior art would deepen, not repair, the gap; trivial also understates novelty's core test.
distractorExplanations.c: Celebrate is tone, not analysis; cosmetic mislabels a novelty issue as merely decorative.
distractorExplanations.d: Examiners do not invent prior art; imaginary undercuts the idea that the art may actually explain the defect.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-006.prompt: The zoning board's move to _______ the nightclub variance was widely read as an attempt to _______ a lawsuit from residents before it was filed.

options.a: approve ... provoke
options.b: table ... forestall
options.c: publicize ... inflame
options.d: expand ... welcome

gre-readiness-check-verbal-006.explanation: To table a matter is to set it aside; to forestall is to head off an event in advance. Delaying the variance is a coherent tactic for preventing a suit.

distractorExplanations.a: Approving a contested variance would more likely provoke a suit than prevent one.
distractorExplanations.c: Publicizing the variance would typically raise, not lower, the chance of litigation.
distractorExplanations.d: Expanding the variance and welcoming a lawsuit invert the defensive 'before it was filed' goal.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-007.prompt: Although the archive's new finding aid was meant to _______ retrieval, staff soon reported that nested subseries _______ even routine searches.

options.a: slow ... accelerated
options.b: preserve ... digitized
options.c: expedite ... hampered
options.d: complicate ... simplified

gre-readiness-check-verbal-007.explanation: Although sets intended benefit against actual harm. Expedite (speed up) versus hampered (held back) is the needed reversal around the steep nested structure.

distractorExplanations.a: A finding aid is not designed to slow retrieval, and accelerated contradicts the complaint.
distractorExplanations.b: Preserve and digitized name conservation work, not the speed contrast in the stem.
distractorExplanations.d: Designers would not aim to complicate retrieval, and simplified clashes with the reported trouble.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-008.prompt: Excavators at an inland tumulus found glass beads whose chemical signature matches Levantine coastal furnaces. The tumulus had been treated as a closed pastoral cemetery with no long-distance exchange. The find most reasonably suggests that

options.a: the tumulus was actually a seaport misplotted on modern maps
options.b: the beads were poured on-site from local river sand
options.c: the cemetery was emptied before any grave goods arrived
options.d: exchange reached farther inland than the isolation model allowed

gre-readiness-check-verbal-008.explanation: Coastal-furnace chemistry in an inland cemetery undercuts the closed-exchange model. The economical inference is a longer-range network, not a relocated coastline or local sand-melt.

distractorExplanations.a: Inland location is given; the beads do not relocate the site to the sea.
distractorExplanations.b: A Levantine furnace signature is evidence against a purely local melt from river sand.
distractorExplanations.c: Emptying the cemetery would not explain how coastal beads entered the graves.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-009.prompt: An agronomy essay says no-till methods 'took root among tenant growers only after three wet harvests.' Took root most nearly means

options.a: became established in ordinary practice
options.b: were banned by the county extension office
options.c: failed because roots could not penetrate clay
options.d: required growers to plant only deep-rooted crops

gre-readiness-check-verbal-009.explanation: Figurative took root means a practice became settled. The time clause (after wet harvests) marks adoption, not a botanical failure or a ban.

distractorExplanations.b: A ban is the opposite of a method becoming common among tenants.
distractorExplanations.c: Reads root literally as plant anatomy; the essay is about farming practice spreading.
distractorExplanations.d: Invented crop rule; took root does not mean switching to deep-rooted species.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-010.prompt: The juror's written opinion was so _______ that clerks could not tell whether she meant to affirm or reverse, because each apparent holding was immediately _______ by a contrary aside.

options.a: effusive ... corroborated
options.b: equivocal ... undercut
options.c: scathing ... buttressed
options.d: laconic ... ignored

gre-readiness-check-verbal-010.explanation: Uncertainty about affirm-versus-reverse plus asides that cancel holdings describes an equivocal opinion whose points are undercut as they appear.

distractorExplanations.a: Effusive praise would not hide the disposition; corroborated would strengthen, not cancel, holdings.
distractorExplanations.c: A scathing opinion usually makes its stance obvious; buttressed also fails the canceling-aside logic.
distractorExplanations.d: Brevity alone does not produce contradiction; ignored asides would not create the clerks' confusion.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-011.prompt: The labor economist's brief was both _______ and _______, packing regression tables yet remaining readable to organizers without statistics coursework.

options.a: encyclopedic ... opaque
options.b: cursory ... labyrinthine
options.c: exacting ... lucid
options.d: partisan ... cryptic

gre-readiness-check-verbal-011.explanation: Detailed tables plus accessibility to non-statisticians pair exacting (demanding, thorough) with lucid (clear). The 'yet' is additive, not adversarial.

distractorExplanations.a: Opaque contradicts readability for organizers without stats training.
distractorExplanations.b: Cursory clashes with packed tables; labyrinthine would block, not help, those readers.
distractorExplanations.d: Partisan is unsupported; cryptic again contradicts the accessibility clause.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-012.prompt: Rather than _______ the dispute, the mediator's recap _______ it by naming three new alleged breaches nobody had put on the agenda.

options.a: ignore ... illuminate
options.b: sidestep ... simplify
options.c: concede ... settle
options.d: clarify ... compound

gre-readiness-check-verbal-012.explanation: Rather than plus extra alleged breaches means the recap failed to make the fight clearer and instead added complexity. Clarify versus compound is that contrast.

distractorExplanations.a: Illuminate would reduce fog; new unagendized breaches do the opposite.
distractorExplanations.b: Simplify contradicts the addition of fresh alleged breaches.
distractorExplanations.c: Settle is the opposite of widening the docket; concede also misses the 'new variables' effect.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-013.prompt: Sherds from a river terrace kiln show firing temperatures once credited only to workshops dated two centuries later. The terrace occupation otherwise looks early. This evidence most strongly supports which conclusion?

options.a: The chronology of high-fire ceramics in the valley may need revision.
options.b: River terraces were never used for kilns anywhere in the whole region.
options.c: The sherds must have been dumped by nineteenth-century antiquarians.
options.d: Kiln archaeology has become cheaper in the last five years.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-013.explanation: High-fire marks in an early occupation undercut a later-only timeline. The tight inference is chronological revision, not a ban on terrace kilns or a cost of methods.

distractorExplanations.b: One terrace kiln cannot show terraces were never used for firing.
distractorExplanations.c: Antiquarian dumping is an unstated extra story, not what the temperature evidence itself supports.
distractorExplanations.d: Method cost is outside the passage; the issue is when high-fire skill existed.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-014.prompt: A transport historian writes that later rail mergers showed 'path dependence': yesterday's gauge choices still dictated today's switching yards. Path dependence most nearly means

options.a: engineers always pick the technically optimal gauge
options.b: early decisions constrain later options even when better designs exist
options.c: all rail lines eventually convert to a single world standard
options.d: switching yards are independent of any prior track decisions

gre-readiness-check-verbal-014.explanation: Path dependence is lock-in: prior choices (here, gauge) keep shaping later infrastructure even if a cleaner design is now imaginable.

distractorExplanations.a: Optimal-gauge myth is the opposite of being stuck with yesterday's choice.
distractorExplanations.c: Global conversion is a forecast the term does not make.
distractorExplanations.d: Independence from prior track decisions denies the historian's claim.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-015.prompt: Reviewers praised the memoir's _______ chronology, which _______ the usual cradle-to-grave order by looping through the same weekend from three relatives' memories.

options.a: stock ... ratified
options.b: foreseeable ... flouted
options.c: inventive ... upended
options.d: linear ... tidied

gre-readiness-check-verbal-015.explanation: A looped, multi-perspective weekend is an inventive structure that upends linear life-story convention.

distractorExplanations.a: Stock plus ratified would describe a conventional order, not a looped weekend.
distractorExplanations.b: Foreseeable undercuts the praise for an unusual structure, even if flouted partly fits.
distractorExplanations.d: Linear and tidied describe the convention being broken, not the memoir as written.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-016.prompt: The treaty's operative clause was left deliberately _______, so later cabinets could stretch it toward whichever alliance they happened to need.

options.a: pellucid
options.b: trenchant
options.c: hortatory
options.d: oracular

gre-readiness-check-verbal-016.explanation: Oracular language is riddling and open-ended, which is exactly what lets later cabinets stretch a clause. The purpose clause ('so later cabinets could') requires vagueness, not clarity.

distractorExplanations.a: Pellucid means crystal-clear; that would block opportunistic stretching.
distractorExplanations.b: Trenchant means sharply decisive; it would pin meaning down, not loosen it.
distractorExplanations.c: Hortatory means exhorting; tone of urging is not the same as interpretive looseness.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-017.prompt: The field linguist's sketch of the river pidgin was unusually _______, because the pronoun system _______ the tidy kinship grids in the region's standard grammars.

options.a: striking ... eluded
options.b: rigid ... duplicated
options.c: banal ... ratified
options.d: familiar ... mirrored

gre-readiness-check-verbal-017.explanation: Unusually plus a mismatch with standard grids calls for a striking description of a system that eluded (escaped) those grids.

distractorExplanations.b: A rigid copy of existing grids would not be unusual or hard to classify.
distractorExplanations.c: Banal ratification of standard grammars is the opposite of a notable mismatch.
distractorExplanations.d: Familiar mirroring again denies that the pidgin escaped the tidy grids.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-018.prompt: A lighting study compared 40 warehouses that installed amber night LEDs with 40 that kept blue-white lamps, matching building age and shift length. Night-shift workers under amber light posted higher melatonin readings at 3 a.m. Which conclusion is most directly supported?

options.a: Amber LEDs are the cheapest way to raise warehouse output.
options.b: Night spectrum is associated with higher melatonin when other site factors are matched.
options.c: All blue-white lamps should be outlawed in every workplace.
options.d: Melatonin differences prove amber light cures insomnia.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-018.explanation: The design matches sites and reports a melatonin contrast by lamp spectrum. That supports an association under controls, not cost rankings, a total ban, or a clinical cure.

distractorExplanations.a: The study did not measure cost or output, only melatonin at 3 a.m.
distractorExplanations.c: A matched warehouse sample cannot justify outlawing every blue-white lamp.
distractorExplanations.d: Melatonin at one hour is not evidence that amber light treats insomnia.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-019.prompt: Despite a reputation for _______ ballets that left first-time audiences bewildered, the choreographer's new suite was unexpectedly _______, with motifs a casual listener could hum on the way out.

options.a: approachable ... intricate
options.b: recondite ... tuneful
options.c: abstruse ... approachable
options.d: hackneyed ... radical

gre-readiness-check-verbal-019.explanation: Despite plus bewildered first-timers versus hummable motifs needs abstruse (hard to penetrate) contrasted with approachable.

distractorExplanations.a: Reverses the contrast: an approachable reputation would not surprise with intricate new work, and intricate fights the humming clause.
distractorExplanations.b: Recondite fits the reputation, but tuneful is narrower than the accessibility claimed for casual listeners.
distractorExplanations.d: Hackneyed versus radical is the wrong polarity for a reputation of bewildering difficulty.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-020.prompt: Oasis weigh-house ledgers in three scripts list silk bolts and coin types two centuries before textbooks date trans-desert bulk trade. Which inference is most reasonable?

options.a: Caravans already used magnetic compasses on every crossing.
options.b: Silk was cheaper in oases than in later imperial markets.
options.c: The ledgers are the first known bills of international credit.
options.d: Standard dates for desert bulk trade may be too late.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-020.explanation: Dated bulk-trade lists earlier than the textbook horizon most directly imply the chronology may run too late. Compass use, relative prices, and 'first credit' are extra claims.

distractorExplanations.a: Ledgers of goods and coin do not document navigation instruments.
distractorExplanations.b: No price comparison to later markets is given.
distractorExplanations.c: Listing transactions is not proof these were the earliest credit instruments.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-021.prompt: The logician's proof was so _______ that referees, after a full recitation of steps, still could not locate an _______ lemma.

options.a: watertight ... assailable
options.b: careful ... defensible
options.c: tangled ... vulnerable
options.d: thin ... unpersuasive

gre-readiness-check-verbal-021.explanation: Referees who cannot find a weak lemma after checking every step are facing a watertight proof with no assailable (attackable) piece.

distractorExplanations.b: They would not struggle to find defensible lemmas; they would struggle to find indefensible ones.
distractorExplanations.c: A tangled proof might hide gaps, but it would not make vulnerable lemmas scarce.
distractorExplanations.d: A thin proof is easy to attack; unpersuasive lemmas are the holes, which would be easy to locate.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-022.prompt: A rare tin-lead solder recipe, once treated as unique to one river delta foundry, appears in slag from three upland smithies dated to the same generation. The recipe is otherwise almost unattested. Which hypothesis is best supported?

options.a: Each smithy invented the alloy separately from identical ores.
options.b: Craft knowledge of that solder traveled with people farther than assumed.
options.c: All three radiocarbon dates must be discarded as lab error.
options.d: Modern chemists cannot tell tin-lead solders apart at all.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-022.explanation: A rare, same-generation recipe in distant smithies most economically implies movement of people or recipes, not three independent inventions or a collapse of dating and chemistry.

distractorExplanations.a: Independent invention of an otherwise unattested recipe in three places at once is the less economical story.
distractorExplanations.c: Nothing in the stem shows the dates are lab errors; the puzzle is geographic spread.
distractorExplanations.d: The analysis did distinguish the recipe; a claim that chemists cannot tell solders apart contradicts that.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-023.prompt: In a public-finance essay, the author says a new bond issue risked 'crowding out' private plant loans. Crowding out most nearly means

options.a: the government would physically occupy factory floors
options.b: private borrowers would enjoy cheaper credit than before
options.c: public borrowing would soak up credit, raising private loan costs
options.d: bond buyers would be required to work in the plants they funded

gre-readiness-check-verbal-023.explanation: Crowding out is the fiscal claim that public borrowing absorbs loanable funds, lifting rates and squeezing private investment. That is the essay's worry about the bond issue.

distractorExplanations.a: Literal occupation of factory floors is not the credit-market sense of the term.
distractorExplanations.b: Cheaper private credit is the opposite of being crowded out.
distractorExplanations.d: Labor requirements for bondholders are unrelated to the interest-rate channel.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-024.prompt: The gallery's wall text was intentionally _______, because the curator thought _______ period labels would let viewers judge the disputed canvases without a borrowed storyline.

options.a: polemical ... stressing
options.b: didactic ... multiplying
options.c: encyclopedic ... deleting
options.d: spare ... muting

gre-readiness-check-verbal-024.explanation: Independent judgment without a borrowed storyline requires sparse text that mutes (tones down) period labels rather than preaching a narrative.

distractorExplanations.a: Polemical, stressing labels would impose a storyline, the opposite of the curator's aim.
distractorExplanations.b: Didactic multiplying of labels increases guidance, not viewer autonomy.
distractorExplanations.c: Encyclopedic wall text is the opposite of withholding context, even if deleting is tempting.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-025.prompt: A coding academy found that students who used drop-in office hours were 35% more likely to receive intern offers. Those same students already had higher take-home scores and larger alumni contact lists before the hours existed. Which conclusion is most warranted?

options.a: Offer gaps may partly reflect who already sought help and contacts.
options.b: Only the highest scorers should be allowed into office hours.
options.c: Office hours alone cause intern offers, independent of prior skill.
options.d: Academies should drop office hours because they help only the strong.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-025.explanation: Preexisting scores and networks mean the offer gap may be selection, not a pure office-hour effect. That is the cautious, data-faithful reading.

distractorExplanations.b: Turns a selection pattern into a restriction policy the study does not test.
distractorExplanations.c: Asserts causation the baseline differences specifically undermine.
distractorExplanations.d: Overreads mixed selection evidence as a reason to abolish help hours.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-026.prompt: Peers called the excavator's trench logs _______ because she _______ even charcoal flecks others would have swept aside.

options.a: bloated ... discarded
options.b: model ... recorded
options.c: sketchy ... conserved
options.d: radical ... overlooked

gre-readiness-check-verbal-026.explanation: Admiration for catching tiny flecks fits model (exemplary) logs that recorded those flecks rather than tossing them.

distractorExplanations.a: Discarding flecks cannot be what peers admired in the logs.
distractorExplanations.c: Sketchy logs contradict praised thoroughness, even if conserved sounds careful.
distractorExplanations.d: Overlooked flecks contradicts the claim she caught what others missed.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-027.prompt: Eight ports that added commuter ferries saw 20% fewer peak car trips under 4 miles and 12% fewer crash injuries per capita than eight matched ports without ferries, after controlling for population and weather. Which conclusion is most reasonable?

options.a: Ferries are the single best congestion cure in every coastal city.
options.b: Ferries will end private car ownership in harbor towns.
options.c: Ferry ports in the sample had milder short-trip crash rates.
options.d: Ferry programs always pay for themselves within one year.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-027.explanation: Fewer short car trips plus fewer injuries in matched ferry ports support a milder short-trip crash environment in that sample—not a global ranking, an end to cars, or a one-year payback.

distractorExplanations.a: No comparison to other congestion tools, so 'single best' is unsupported.
distractorExplanations.b: A 20% drop in some short trips does not abolish car ownership.
distractorExplanations.d: No cost or revenue figures appear, so payback cannot be inferred.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-028.prompt: Because the playwright was known for psychologically layered roles, ticket buyers found the new script especially _______ if they wanted _______ figures instead of types.

options.a: easy ... shallow
options.b: dismaying ... intricate
options.c: taxing ... stock
options.d: attractive ... shaded

gre-readiness-check-verbal-028.explanation: A reputation for layered roles would make the script attractive to people hunting shaded (nuanced) figures rather than types.

distractorExplanations.a: Shallow figures are types, the opposite of what those buyers want.
distractorExplanations.b: Buyers seeking intricate roles would not be dismayed by a writer known for them.
distractorExplanations.c: Stock figures are stereotypes; taxing also misreads the audience that wants complexity.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-029.prompt: A year-long study found open-plan clerks had higher afternoon cortisol, 28% more self-reported sleep breaks, and 20% more sick days than clerks in enclosed rooms, though open-plan desks came with an 8% pay premium. What can most reasonably be inferred?

options.a: Open-plan work coincided with higher measured stress markers.
options.b: The pay premium fully offsets any health cost of office noise.
options.c: Enclosed-room clerks produce more counted output per hour.
options.d: Firms must abolish open plans to cut insurance bills.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-029.explanation: Higher cortisol, more sleep breaks, and more sick days are the measured stress cluster. Pay-offset, productivity, and mandatory abolition go beyond those measures.

distractorExplanations.b: No health-cost accounting is given against the 8% premium.
distractorExplanations.c: Productivity per hour was never measured, so a yield ranking cannot be drawn from cortisol and sick days.
distractorExplanations.d: Insurance bills and a duty to abolish layouts are policy leaps, not findings.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-030.prompt: When a tax economist says a levy creates 'deadweight loss,' she most nearly means the tax

options.a: spreads the same tax burden equally across every mapped region
options.b: shrinks mutually beneficial trades below the no-tax volume
options.c: balances the budget by matching spending to receipts
options.d: standardizes product rules so all firms face one code

gre-readiness-check-verbal-030.explanation: Deadweight loss is the surplus destroyed when a tax wedges price from cost and some trades that would have happened no longer do.

distractorExplanations.a: Geographic equality of burden is incidence geography, not deadweight loss.
distractorExplanations.c: Budget balance is a fiscal identity, not the efficiency triangle.
distractorExplanations.d: Product-rule standardization is regulation, not the tax wedge.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-031.prompt: Even critics who rejected the trial's conclusions conceded that the statistician's protocol was so _______ that its sampling frame looked _______.

options.a: sloppy ... dubious
options.b: novel ... obsolete
options.c: stringent ... painstaking
options.d: polarizing ... prejudicial

gre-readiness-check-verbal-031.explanation: Concession despite disagreement requires a positive pair: a stringent protocol whose frame looks painstaking (carefully thorough).

distractorExplanations.a: Critics would not concede sloppiness as a virtue of the design.
distractorExplanations.b: Novel and obsolete cancel each other; obsolete is not a conceded strength.
distractorExplanations.d: Prejudicial is a slant they would attack, not a quality they would grant.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-032.prompt: In 40 counties, tracts with median income under $32,000 had 55% fewer 24-hour pharmacies per capita and residents traveled 1.9 miles farther for a fill, spending a larger share of monthly budgets on that trip. Which conclusion is strongest?

options.a: Low-income residents prefer gas-station pain relievers to pharmacies.
options.b: Chains avoid poor tracts solely because of thinner margins.
options.c: County boards designed the map to punish poor tracts on purpose.
options.d: Distance and income together worsen pharmacy access in those tracts.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-032.explanation: Fewer pharmacies plus longer, costlier trips describe stacked geographic and economic barriers. Preferences, chain motives, and intentional punishment are not in the data.

distractorExplanations.a: No preference data appear—only access and travel cost.
distractorExplanations.b: Margins and chain strategy are unmeasured causes.
distractorExplanations.c: Disparities do not by themselves prove purposeful board design.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-033.prompt: The nominee's hearing answers showed such _______ that reporters could not extract a yes or no, because she _______ each firm clause with a softening rider.

options.a: evasiveness ... blunted
options.b: lucidity ... fortified
options.c: fervor ... spotlighted
options.d: terseness ... lengthened

gre-readiness-check-verbal-033.explanation: No extractable yes/no plus softening riders is evasiveness that blunts (dulls) otherwise firm clauses.

distractorExplanations.b: Lucidity would yield a clear yes or no; fortified clauses would be firmer, not softer.
distractorExplanations.c: Fervor does not explain unreadable positions; spotlighting would make clauses clearer.
distractorExplanations.d: Terseness is brevity, not waffle; lengthened with riders is closer, but the first blank still fails.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-034.prompt: In timed chess, players with 20+ years of tournament play chose quieter lines 74% of the time versus 48% for novices. Over a simulated match set, veterans' lines scored only 9% fewer points but had 35% fewer lost-on-time collapses. Which inference is most reasonable?

options.a: Veterans cannot calculate tactics as well as novices.
options.b: Long practice may trade a little peak score for fewer time disasters.
options.c: Novices are simply better at converting winning positions.
options.d: Quiet lines always dominate sharp lines in every time control.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-034.explanation: Slightly lower point yield with far fewer time collapses is a risk-stability tradeoff consistent with accumulated practical judgment, not a claim about raw calculating power.

distractorExplanations.a: No calculation test is reported; quieter lines are a choice, not a proven deficit.
distractorExplanations.c: Novices' extra points come with more time losses, so 'simply better' oversimplifies.
distractorExplanations.d: Always/every time control overgeneralizes one simulated set.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-035.prompt: A critic of appellate dissents calls some footnotes 'purposely occluded.' She most likely means the writers

options.a: left the notes confusing by accident after a rushed cite check
options.b: copied earlier cases without any quotation marks
options.c: chose dense wording to force slower, harder reading
options.d: cared only about page design, not about legal meaning

gre-readiness-check-verbal-035.explanation: Purposely plus occluded (blocked from easy view) means intentional density that slows interpretation—an artistic or strategic opacity, not accident or layout fetish.

distractorExplanations.a: Purposely rules out accident after a rushed cite check.
distractorExplanations.b: Occlusion is about clarity of meaning, not missing quotation marks.
distractorExplanations.d: Page design is unrelated to occluded wording as a reading challenge.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-036.prompt: The diplomat's reading of the joint communiqué was unusually _______, enabling her to _______ the quarrel buried under ritual adjectives of friendship.

options.a: glib ... bury
options.b: exhaustive ... skip
options.c: partisan ... hide
options.d: astute ... detect

gre-readiness-check-verbal-036.explanation: Spotting a quarrel under friendship adjectives is astute reading that detects what the ritual language hides.

distractorExplanations.a: Glib plus bury would hide the quarrel further, not surface it.
distractorExplanations.b: Skip the quarrel contradicts finding it; exhaustive also does not force detection.
distractorExplanations.c: Hide repeats the communiqué's own masking, the opposite of the diplomat's feat.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-037.prompt: Students who used the campus studio after midnight had GPAs 0.3 points lower than daytime-only users, yet they also staffed more ensemble gigs and scored higher on group sight-reading. Which conclusion is most reasonable?

options.a: Late studio use tracks mixed academic and collaborative outcomes.
options.b: The campus studio should close at 10 p.m. to maximize GPA alone.
options.c: Midnight hours directly cause the GPA gap with no other factors.
options.d: Gig work erases any GPA difference tied to late hours.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-037.explanation: Lower GPA alongside stronger ensemble and sight-reading scores is a mixed pattern, not a single-cause story or a policy to shut the building.

distractorExplanations.b: Maximizing GPA alone ignores documented collaborative gains.
distractorExplanations.c: Correlation with late hours is not proof of exclusive causation.
distractorExplanations.d: The GPA gap is reported; gigs do not erase it.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-038.prompt: The survey team's sampling grid was so _______ that they could _______ seasonal fish pulses earlier crews had written off as noise.

options.a: scattershot ... notice
options.b: methodical ... isolate
options.c: routine ... miss
options.d: daring ... overlook

gre-readiness-check-verbal-038.explanation: Catching pulses others dismissed as noise requires a methodical grid that can isolate (pick out) those pulses.

distractorExplanations.a: A scattershot grid is unlikely to recover faint seasonal structure.
distractorExplanations.c: Routine work that misses pulses is what the earlier crews already did.
distractorExplanations.d: Overlook directly contradicts recovering the pulses.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-039.prompt: City-park bat colonies had 30% more light-related roost abandonments than rural barns, but they also rebounded 25% faster after heat waves and hosted 18% more insect-prey species; those parks had weekly volunteer counts and nest-box repairs. What is the soundest conclusion?

options.a: City parks are uniformly worse habitat and should be avoided.
options.b: Urban bats are naturally hardier, with no role for human care.
options.c: Urban proximity brought both extra stress and extra stewardship.
options.d: Volunteer roost programs have no demonstrated link to rebound speed.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-039.explanation: More abandonments plus faster rebound and richer prey, alongside volunteer care, describe mixed stress and protection—not uniform harm or purely natural toughness.

distractorExplanations.a: Ignores faster rebound and higher prey diversity in the parks.
distractorExplanations.b: Credits only 'natural' hardiness and erases the mentioned nest-box work.
distractorExplanations.d: The passage flags volunteer counts and repairs as a plausible aid to rebound.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-040.prompt: In a used-textbook market, an economist says 'adverse selection' worsened after the university stopped grading condition. She most likely means

options.a: buyers chased riskier, higher-yield speculative textbook editions
options.b: students demanded prettier covers when tuition rose
options.c: printers raised paper quality to keep market share
options.d: hidden poor-condition books drove good copies out of the pool

gre-readiness-check-verbal-040.explanation: Adverse selection is the hidden-quality spiral: when condition is unobservable, lemons remain and better copies withdraw. Stopping condition grades is exactly that information drop.

distractorExplanations.a: Risk-seeking for yield is a finance 'reach for return,' not textbook lemons.
distractorExplanations.b: Cover aesthetics and tuition are not the information-asymmetry mechanism.
distractorExplanations.c: Printers' paper quality is a supply-side quality race, not buyer-seller hidden defects.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-041.prompt: Tagged ibex using high salt licks finished the seasonal move 6 days sooner than valley-lick herds despite 12 extra kilometers, arrived with 14% better body scores, and had 19% higher kid survival, though high licks sat nearer climbing routes. Which conclusion is strongest?

options.a: Time and condition gains may offset extra distance and climb risk.
options.b: High salt licks are better for every ibex population in every range.
options.c: Valley licks should be closed so all herds are forced uphill.
options.d: Climbing routes have no bearing on whether kids survive.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-041.explanation: Faster arrival, better condition, and higher kid survival against extra kilometers and climb exposure support a possible offset, not a universal ranking or a closure order.

distractorExplanations.b: 'Every population in every range' overgeneralizes one tagged sample.
distractorExplanations.c: Forcing all herds uphill ignores the stated climb risks.
distractorExplanations.d: The stem treats climbing routes as a relevant exposure, not a null factor.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-042.prompt: The ceramicist's map of kiln stamps was unusually _______, letting her _______ workshop links that earlier catalogs missed by sorting only by vessel shape.

options.a: thin ... conceal
options.b: wide-ranging ... spot
options.c: skewed ... erase
options.d: habitual ... copy

gre-readiness-check-verbal-042.explanation: Going beyond shape-only catalogs to recover missed workshop links is a wide-ranging map that spots those links.

distractorExplanations.a: A thin map that hides links is the earlier failure, not her advance.
distractorExplanations.c: Erase links is the opposite of recovering them; skewed is unearned.
distractorExplanations.d: Habitual copying of old catalogs would reproduce the shape-only blind spot.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-043.prompt: Pianists who drilled etudes in four 10-minute bursts retained 22% more passages at one week than those who crammed 40 minutes at once, but the massed group scored higher on a same-day speed trial. Which inference is most reasonable?

options.a: Spaced practice is always best for every musical skill.
options.b: Massed cramming should be banned from all conservatories.
options.c: Retention and same-day speed may peak under different schedules.
options.d: Week-later memory is the only outcome that matters in performance.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-043.explanation: Spaced bursts win delayed retention; massed wins same-day speed. That split implies different schedules can serve different goals.

distractorExplanations.a: 'Always/every skill' ignores the massed group's same-day speed edge.
distractorExplanations.b: A ban does not follow from a mixed outcome pattern.
distractorExplanations.d: The study itself treats same-day speed as a real second outcome.

gre-readiness-check-verbal-044.prompt: A fiction critic calls a narrator 'unreliable' after the diary dates contradict the same speaker's later boasts. She most likely means the narrator

options.a: uses only recycled paper for ethical reasons
options.b: refuses any invented place-names whatsoever
options.c: itemizes every expense so readers can audit the plot
options.d: cannot be taken at face value because the story undercuts the teller

gre-readiness-check-verbal-044.explanation: Unreliable narration is a gap between teller and tale. Contradictory dates versus boasts are internal undercutting, not ethics of paper, toponyms, or expense lists.

distractorExplanations.a: Confuses narrative reliability with environmental ethics of stationery.
distractorExplanations.b: Place-name invention is world-building, not the diary-versus-boast problem.
distractorExplanations.c: Literal 'audit' of expenses misses the literary sense of a compromised speaker.
